item.title: Kuma River Rafting — Guide
item.description: The Kuma River, flowing through the Hitoyoshi valley in the mountains near the Kagoshima–Kumamoto border, is renowned as one of the three fastest-flowing rivers in Japan, making it a premier destination for river adventure. Its lively rapids and clear waters, set amid green mountains, are ideal for exhilarating white-water rafting trips in the warmer months, with guided tours suitable for beginners, families and thrill-seekers who paddle together through the rapids and calmer pools.

item.title: Mangrove Kayaking on Iriomote — Guide
item.description: Iriomote Island, the largest of the Yaeyama Islands and one of Japan’s last great wildernesses, is around 90% covered in dense subtropical jungle and mangrove forest — earning it the nickname ‘the Galapagos of the East’. Kayaking through its mangrove-lined rivers is the classic way to experience this remarkable natural environment. Guided tours paddle up winding tidal rivers such as the Urauchi and Nakama, gliding quietly between towering mangrove trees whose tangled roots arch over the water, past lush jungle alive with birds, crabs and other wildlife.

item.title: River Kayaking & Canoeing in Miyazaki — Guide
item.description: Miyazaki’s mountainous interior is laced with beautiful, clear rivers that make superb settings for kayaking and canoeing. On the scenic Gokase River near Takachiho and other inland waterways, guided tours let paddlers glide across calm, emerald-green stretches of water framed by forested gorges, cliffs and greenery, taking in the pristine scenery from the water at a gentle pace. Suitable for beginners, families and experienced paddlers alike, the tours typically provide all equipment and a guide, and range from relaxing flat-water paddles on rivers and reservoirs to more adventurous stretches.

item.title: Ryugado Cave: Kochi's Limestone Wonder — Guide
item.description: Ryugado is counted among Japan’s three great limestone caves, a spectacular cavern carved over a million and a half years into the hills of eastern Kochi. A well-lit walking route of around a kilometre leads through soaring chambers past a wealth of formations — stalactites, flowstone curtains, an underground waterfall and pools — with the added fascination of ancient traces showing that people lived at the cave mouth some two thousand years ago.

item.title: Sandboarding on the Tottori Dunes — Guide
item.description: Sandboarding — snowboarding’s desert cousin — is one of the most fun and accessible activities at the Tottori Sand Dunes. You strap onto a board and slide down the steep slip-face of a dune, with the soft sand making for gentle, forgiving landings that suit total beginners and children. Local operators run guided lessons that include the board, basic instruction and the walk back up, on a slope steep enough to be genuinely exciting.

item.title: River Rafting in Wakayama: Rapids Through the Kii Gorges — Guide
item.description: The steep, forested gorges of the Kii Peninsula channel a series of fast, remarkably clear rivers that make Wakayama one of the best river-sports destinations in western Japan. Guided rafting trips run through rapids framed by cliffs and cedar forest, with operators offering everything from gentle family-friendly floats to genuinely exciting whitewater, while canyoning and the traditional log-raft rides of the Kitayama River add further variety. The water is famously clear, the scenery is superb, and the mountain setting keeps things cool through the summer months when trips are at their peak.

item.title: Matsushima Bay Kayaking: Paddle Among the Pine Islands — Guide
item.description: Sea kayaking through Matsushima Bay offers an entirely different perspective on one of Japan’s Three Great Views — paddling at water level between the bay’s roughly 260 pine-covered islets, gliding through narrow channels and sea caves the tour boats can’t reach. Guided tours suit all experience levels, with calm, sheltered waters ideal for first-time kayakers, and sunrise or sunset paddles offering especially striking light on the pines and rock formations.
